problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a QR Factorization of a Matrix Given a Matrix With Orthogonal Columns
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093486/assets/9a03ebd899e90c7fc94c302ed43a2f737d0873f10c5aa0677fc1cade33b707ba.png)

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns $\mathbf{q}_1,\mathbf{q}_2$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of $q_{12} \cdot r_{22}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct a matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbf{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by $Q^T,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093486/assets/7599c7b3f9a02ac234da9d6893796dab00f4316ad1260f3e6958966d9cb53371.png)

Finally, $q_{12} \cdot r_{22} = -\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot 3 = -2.$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖} & \frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖} & \frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} & {r}_{13} \\ 0 & {r}_{22} & {r}_{23} \\ 0 & 0 & {r}_{33}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above, where ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is an orthogonal set of vectors. You're given that $‖{v}_{1}‖=3,$ $‖{v}_{2}‖=4,$ $‖{v}_{3}‖=2,$ and that the system of equations below describes the relationship between the columns of $Q$ and the columns of $A.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}={a}_{1} \\ {v}_{2}={a}_{2}-3{v}_{1} \\ {v}_{3}={a}_{3}-5{v}_{1}-2{v}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

What is the value of ${r}_{13}+{r}_{22}+{r}_{33}?$
